_meta.usage: nine-digit number as written on signs: 71 123 45 67, (66) 233-45-67 or +998 65 221 23 45. Type the whole number: a code on its own does not match, so that it can't collide with other countries' codes
_meta.note: Since 2018–2020 all numbers have nine digits: a two-digit code, then seven digits; there is no trunk prefix. Geographic codes are 61–79; 20, 33, 50, 77, 80, 87–99 are mobile or other non-geographic ranges. 36 is left out pending a dated operator or regulator source: goldenpages.uz lists 36 for most of Navoiy Region, but the ITU numbering plan and Ucell's dialing guide list 79, and the 2015 conversion plan on norma.uz maps the old 0436 numbers to 79.
_meta.miss_note: not a geographic Uzbek code: a mobile number (20, 33, 50, 77, 88, 90–99 …), 78 (non-geographic fixed), 55 (VoIP), 36 (listed for Navoiy by goldenpages.uz only; 79 is the code the ITU plan and Ucell give), an old seven-digit local number written without the code, or a number of another country
source: https://www.goldenpages.uz/uzcodes/ (codes by settlement and district, 2026; 70 Tashkent Region)
https://www.ituob.org/issues/1263-en/ (ITU Operational Bulletin 1263, Uzbekistan numbering plan: 79 Navoiy)

99870.note: goldenpages.uz lists 70 for Tashkent Region landlines; en.wikipedia lists 70 as Uzmobile mobile, so a 70 number may also be a mobile phone (any region)

99871.note: the Tashkent city zone also serves numbers in parts of Tashkent Region; most of the region is listed under 70
